note: The authoritative definition of the village's harvestable resource nodes and of the resource uses and sources the code defines (owner, 2026-10-18: Master Resource Node Manifest and Resource Usage Registry). Everything here describes the implemented game; nothing is a new mechanic. Numbers given as strings are balance.json keys (a dotted path into balance.json, e.g. 'animals.boar.meat'), resolved at run time, so this file never restates a tunable number. Read at run time by ResourceNodes (game/scripts/core/resource_nodes.gd) through GameData.resources; validated, and docs/systems/RESOURCE_NODE_MANIFEST.md and RESOURCE_USAGE_REGISTRY.md generated, by tools/check_resources.py.

deposit_tiles.note: Each kind of rock deposit, the paid-atlas tile it is drawn with (village.json layers; tile = atlas 0 + id) and what it gives (B8-008, owner Build 8 playtest). One sprite is one product: an ore-flecked sprite is always a seam of that ore, and a plain grey boulder (tile 1964) is stone. VillageMap.normalise_rocks applies it when the map loads: a seam is drawn with its ore's tile whatever the map data says, a flecked rock with no seam behind it is drawn as a plain boulder, and a worked-out seam is drawn with the hollow tile.

iron_seam.name: Iron seam
iron_seam.where: In the mine north of the village
iron_seam.tool_hint: You need a pickaxe. The smith and the goods merchant sell them, or forge one at the anvil (2 iron bars and a plank).
iron_seam.time_note: A villager works mine_minutes game minutes a unit. The player's swing takes mine_minutes / game_minutes_per_second x 0.6 real seconds, divided by the pickaxe's speed (the rusty pickaxe is slower).

action_cost.note: No stamina. The pickaxe wears 1 a swing; from Mining 4 the player's wears only half the time.

iron_seam.yield_notes: Player only: from Mining 2, a 25% chance of a second unit from the same seam.
iron_seam.total: The sum of the iron seams' amounts in village.json deposits.
iron_seam.regeneration: None: World.mine_unit never refills a seam. Once its ore is out, its grey host rock gives quarry_host_stone stone (balance.json, 20; the stone seam node) and then the cell opens (MIN-B); the ore never comes back.
iron_seam.owner: Nobody: the seams belong to no one (the manor's mining rights are only proposed, ECONOMY_SUSTAINABILITY_PROPOSALS.md P1.2).
iron_seam.npc_note: Miners and labourers (NPCBrain._miner, act "mine") while a buyer has room.
iron_seam.range_note: The cell 0.9 tiles in front of the player, or one of its four neighbours (main.gd _find_target).
iron_seam.risk: Overharvested: the iron seams were worked out on day 10 (seed 1, no player), ECONOMY_SUSTAINABILITY_PROPOSALS.md section 1.

stone_seam.tool_hint: You need a pickaxe. The smith and the goods merchant sell them, or forge one at the anvil (2 iron bars and a plank).

stone_seam.range_note: The cell 0.9 tiles in front of the player, or one of its four neighbours (main.gd _find_target).

boulder.where: Grey boulders standing alone, small and large: in the mine's highland and across the map outside the village (every boulder drawn there, mountain boulders included)
boulder.tool_hint: You need a pickaxe. The smith and the goods merchant sell them, or forge one at the anvil (2 iron bars and a plank).
boulder.time_note: As for every seam: mine_minutes game minutes a unit for a villager; the player's swing is shorter, divided by the pickaxe's speed.

action_cost.note: No stamina. The pickaxe wears 1 a swing.

boulder.yield_notes: Player only: from Mining 2, a 25% chance of a second unit from the same boulder.
boulder.total: uses_small (2) stone from a small boulder, uses (6) from a large one (ResourceNodes.boulder_small: a hash of its cell, about 55% are small); the village's boulders count in the village's stone left (World.quarry_stone_left, Quests.deposit_left) since MIN-B.
boulder.regeneration: None: a boulder broken up is gone for good and its cell is open ground. The change is saved (the village's with the world, the overworld's with Overworld.rock_changes).
boulder.npc_note: MIN-B: villagers quarry the village's boulders for stone by the player's rule (World.nearest_seam offers them beside the seams and host rock to labourers, miners, manor quarry hands and stone contracts); the overworld's are the player's alone (villagers stay in the village).
boulder.range_note: The cell 0.9 tiles in front of the player, or one of its four neighbours (main.gd _find_target).
boulder.risk: Stone is cheap: a boulder breaks into only 2 to 6 stone.

tree.name: Tree
tree.where: The woods west and east of the village and the woodland at its edge, and every tree across the map
tree.tool_hint: You need an axe. The smith and the goods merchant sell them, or forge one at the anvil (2 iron bars and a plank).
tree.time_note: A villager works chop_minutes game minutes a tree. The player's takes chop_minutes / game_minutes_per_second x 0.5 real seconds, divided by the axe's speed, and 30% less from Woodcutting 3.

action_cost.note: No stamina. The axe wears 3 a tree.

tree.yield_notes: World.chop_tree takes balance.json tree_growth.chops blows; the last one calls World.fell, which gives 4 logs once; the player gets 1 more from Woodcutting 2 and (chance tree_growth.sapling_chance) a sapling item (oak_sapling or pine_sapling) to plant. Villagers always get 4 and no sapling. Only a MATURE tree can be felled: saplings, young and growing trees give nothing and say why.
tree.total: 4 logs from each mature tree: the village trees (village.json trees and the map-edge woodland), and any overworld tree, generated or planted.
tree.regeneration: A felled tree is a stump; tree_regrow_seasons later (at dawn) it sprouts a sapling, which grows young, growing and mature by the game clock (balance.json tree_growth, in game days; Trees.sync, computed lazily). The player can also plant saplings (World.plant_tree). Ground bought for building is cleared and never grows again (Property.claim).
tree.owner: Nobody: trees belong to no one.
tree.npc_note: Woodcutters (NPCBrain._woodcutter, act "chop"): the nearest mature tree within 70 tiles nobody has claimed; they fell it in one go and do not replant.
tree.range_note: The trunk or the canopy top above it, in the cell 0.9 tiles in front of the player or one of its four neighbours (World.tree_at, main.gd _find_target).
tree.risk: Pressure, not exhaustion: households burn a log a night (8744 logs a year); grown trees settle at about 208 of 305 and firewood runs short on 16-58 household-nights a year (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md, finding 9).

wheat_field.name: Wheat field
wheat_field.where: The manor's open fields south-east of the village
wheat_field.time_note: The player gathers a handful (harvest_handful) in 2.5 real seconds; a farmer's harvest is 90 game minutes and takes all that is left on the field.

action_cost.note: No stamina, no tool.

wheat_field.yield_notes: The player takes harvest_handful a cycle (less if less is left); a farmer takes the whole crop.
wheat_field.total: field_yield wheat on each ripe field in village.json fields.
wheat_field.regeneration: An emptied field is tilled; its farmer sows it (45 minutes) and it ripens field_grow_seasons later with field_yield wheat (World._on_hour). Only a farmer sows: a field nobody works stays tilled until a manor hand takes it over.
wheat_field.owner: The manor's field; its crop belongs to the farmers who work it (World.field_workers).
wheat_field.theft: Harvesting a worked field is theft from its farmer, seen by anyone in sight, except the wheat a farmer hired the player to cut (quest work_the_harvest, Quests.hired_harvest).
wheat_field.range_note: Any cell of a ripe field: the cell 0.9 tiles in front of the player or one of its four neighbours (main.gd _find_target).
wheat_field.risk: Not at risk: farmers hold surplus grain (14495 wheat by day 365, seed 1; LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md finding 6).

flower_patch.name: Wild flower
flower_patch.where: Meadows, verges and clearings across the map, in the village and outside it (red, purple, yellow and white flowers)
flower_patch.time_note: The player picks one in 1.2 real seconds (no game-time cost); villagers pick them in the evening for their households (B14).

action_cost.note: No stamina, no tool.

flower_patch.yield_notes: 1 flower a plant, all at once (World.pick_plant). Whoever picks it (the player or a villager, not the bear) also recovers one flower_seed with chance propagation.kinds.flower.chance, by a hash of the cell, the day and the world seed (World.propagation_drop, SEED-02/SEED-04); planted, it grows a new flower (World.plant_bush).
flower_patch.total: 1 flower from each ripe plant of this kind: village.json plants (tiles 2656 red, 2657 purple, 2658 yellow, 2659 white) and every flower the overworld generator draws outside the village (Overworld.flower_at).
flower_patch.regeneration: A picked plant is bare; at the dawn plant_regrow_seasons later (provisional) it is ripe again (World._new_day). Plants stay walkable either way. Outside the village the picked flower is saved in Overworld.plant_changes. Wild flowers bear in every season (no plant_seasons entry); picking never removes the plant (perennial).
flower_patch.owner: Nobody: wild plants belong to no one.
flower_patch.npc_note: Adults pick ripe plants within home_production.forage_range of home in the evening (B14, NPCBrain._plan_home_work): flowers until the household can brew poultices at its hearth, berries up to berries_keep for the pantry. SEED-04: a forager keeps the cutting or seed the player's rule gives and stores it in the household's pantry; the household keeps propagation.household_keep of each and takes the rest to the seed seller (the food stall) by cart.
flower_patch.range_note: The plant's own cell or one of its four neighbours (ResourceNodes.node_at); the cell can be walked on.
flower_patch.risk: Not at risk: nobody else uses these. Yields and regrowth are provisional (balance review pending).

apple_tree.name: Apple tree (fruit)
apple_tree.where: The cottagers' orchards: village trees near the houses (one in fruit_trees.orchard_share), and any apple tree planted from a sapling
apple_tree.time_note: The player picks in 1.5 real seconds; villagers work 15 game minutes (B14).

action_cost.note: No stamina, no tool.

apple_tree.yield_notes: A grown apple tree in fruit gives fruit_trees.apple_orchard.yield apples at once (World.pick_fruit). It is felled like any tree for logs and, by chance, an apple sapling (the tree node).
apple_tree.regeneration: Picked bare, it bears again fruit_trees.apple_orchard.regrow_seasons later, but only in its fruiting seasons (summer and autumn): none in winter or spring (Trees.fruit_ripe).
apple_tree.owner: Nobody: orchard trees near the houses are common, like the wild plants.
apple_tree.npc_note: Adults pick a fruiting apple tree near home instead of a berry bush when it is nearer (NPCBrain._plan_home_work, act pick_fruit); apples go into the pantry as food and their surplus to the storefront or the food merchant.
apple_tree.range_note: The tree's trunk cell or the cell above it, faced from beside it (main.gd _find_target).
apple_tree.risk: Few trees, a short fruiting window (seasons are 2 days); yields provisional.

wild_boar.name: Wild boar
wild_boar.where: The woods in the north-west and north-east
wild_boar.tool_hint: Any weapon helps (bare hands do 2 damage). The smith and the goods merchant sell swords, or forge one at the anvil.
wild_boar.time_note: A hunter works hunt_minutes game minutes a kill. The player strikes every 0.6 seconds until the animal's health (animals.boar.hp) is gone.

action_cost.note: No stamina; attacks do not wear the weapon.

wild_boar.yield_notes: A young animal gives half the meat (at least 1) and no hide (Fauna.kill). The player's kill is left as a bag where it fell.
wild_boar.total: animals.boar.start (males, females) in each wood, at most animals.boar.woods_cap a wood.
wild_boar.regeneration: A well-fed adult female with a well-fed adult male in her wood gives a litter every breed_years while the wood is under its cap (Fauna.new_day). Nothing migrates in: a group of one sex never breeds again.
wild_boar.owner: Nobody: wild game belongs to no one.
wild_boar.npc_note: Hunters (NPCBrain._hunter, act "hunt") leave animals.boar.keep adults a wood; bandits poach (act "poach").
wild_boar.range_note: An attack reaches 1.1 tiles around a point 0.8 tiles in front of the player (main.gd attack); hunters within 3 tiles.
wild_boar.risk: Was overharvested to a sex-blind floor of 2 adults (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md finding 8); since B14 nobody takes the last grown male or female of a wood and the hunter leaves wildlife.hunter_spare more, but wolves and bears now hunt boar too.

wild_rabbit.name: Rabbit
wild_rabbit.where: The woods in the north-west and north-east
wild_rabbit.tool_hint: Any weapon helps (bare hands do 2 damage). The smith and the goods merchant sell swords, or forge one at the anvil.
wild_rabbit.time_note: A hunter works hunt_minutes game minutes a kill. Rabbits flee the player within animals.rabbit.flee tiles.

action_cost.note: No stamina; attacks do not wear the weapon.

wild_rabbit.yield_notes: Rabbits have no hide (animals.rabbit.hide is 0) but an adult gives a pelt (animals.rabbit.pelt; PL2-004), tanned to leather at the workbench (tan_pelts) or sold to the tanner or goods merchant. A young one gives at least 1 meat and no pelt.
wild_rabbit.total: animals.rabbit.start (males, females) in each wood, at most animals.rabbit.woods_cap a wood.
wild_rabbit.regeneration: As for boar: litters while a well-fed pair shares the wood and it is under its cap; no migration.
wild_rabbit.owner: Nobody: wild game belongs to no one.
wild_rabbit.npc_note: Hunters leave animals.rabbit.keep adults a wood; bandits poach.
wild_rabbit.range_note: An attack reaches 1.1 tiles around a point 0.8 tiles in front of the player (main.gd attack).
wild_rabbit.risk: Was frozen at 4 adults from about day 10 (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md finding 8); since B14 a breeding pair always remains, but foxes and wolves now hunt rabbits too.

action_cost.note: No stamina; attacks do not wear the weapon.

wild_deer.range_note: An attack reaches 1.1 tiles around a point 0.8 tiles in front of the player (main.gd attack).
wild_deer.risk: Prey of wolves and bears as well as the hunter (B14); provisional numbers, watch the 20-day wildlife test.

wild_fox.npc_note: The village hunter leaves it alone (animals.fox.game is false); only the player hunts it.

wild_fox.risk: Takes pen chickens at night (wildlife.fox_raid_chance_per_hour); numbers provisional (B14).

wild_bear.name: Bear
wild_bear.tool_hint: Any weapon helps (bare hands do 2 damage). The smith and the goods merchant sell swords, or forge one at the anvil.
wild_bear.time_note: A bear struck fights back, biting for animals.bear.bite; a starving one goes for a person alone in its wood. It eats ripe berries near its wood first.

action_cost.note: No stamina; attacks do not wear the weapon.

wild_bear.yield_notes: A young bear gives half the meat and no hide. Bears are tough (animals.bear.hp).
wild_bear.total: animals.bear.start (males, females) in each wood it lives in (animals.bear.only), at most animals.bear.woods_cap a wood.
wild_bear.regeneration: Litters while a well-fed pair shares the wood and it is under its cap; nobody takes the last grown male or female of a wood (Fauna.spare).
wild_bear.owner: Nobody: wild game belongs to no one.
wild_bear.npc_note: The village hunter leaves it alone (animals.bear.game is false); only the player hunts it.
wild_bear.range_note: An attack reaches 1.1 tiles around a point 0.8 tiles in front of the player (main.gd attack).

wild_bird.name: Bird
wild_bird.where: The woods in the north-west and north-east
wild_bird.tool_hint: Any weapon helps (bare hands do 2 damage). The smith and the goods merchant sell swords, or forge one at the anvil.
wild_bird.time_note: Birds flee within animals.bird.flee tiles; foxes take them.

action_cost.note: No stamina; attacks do not wear the weapon.

wild_bird.yield_notes: A bird gives a feather and no meat (animals.bird.meat is 0).
wild_bird.total: animals.bird.start (males, females) in each wood, at most animals.bird.woods_cap a wood.
wild_bird.regeneration: Litters while a well-fed pair shares the wood and it is under its cap; nobody takes the last grown male or female of a wood (Fauna.spare).
wild_bird.owner: Nobody: wild game belongs to no one.
wild_bird.npc_note: Hunters leave animals.bird.keep + wildlife.hunter_spare a wood; wolves, foxes and bears hunt it too (Fauna._predate).
wild_bird.range_note: An attack reaches 1.1 tiles around a point 0.8 tiles in front of the player (main.gd attack).

cow_pen.name: Cows
cow_pen.where: The cow pen south of the village
cow_pen.tool_hint: Not yours to take: the animals are their keeper's.
cow_pen.time_note: The keeper's slaughter is 30 game minutes.

action_cost.note: The keeper feeds the pen animals.cow.feed wheat a meal.

cow_pen.yield_notes: A young animal gives half the meat and no hide.
cow_pen.total: animals.cow.start in the pen, at most animals.cow.pen_cap.
cow_pen.regeneration: Litters while a well-fed pair shares the pen and it is under its cap; animals die unfed.
cow_pen.owner: The manor's pen, let to its keeper (a farmer); the animals are the keeper's.
cow_pen.theft: The player killing one is a crime against the keeper (main.gd _hit_animal).
cow_pen.npc_note: The keeper slaughters the surplus above animals.cow.keep, or culls when short of feed (NPCBrain._keeper, act "slaughter").
cow_pen.risk: Not at risk: pens hold at about their caps (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md).

horse_pen.name: Horses
horse_pen.where: The player's own horse pen (bought from the visiting caravan)
horse_pen.tool_hint: Only your own horse stands in a horse pen.
horse_pen.time_note: As for any pen animal: 30 game minutes.

action_cost.note: The player feeds the horse animals.horse.feed wheat a meal at the pen's gate.

horse_pen.yield_notes: A young animal gives half the meat and no hide.
horse_pen.regeneration: None: a horse is bought again from the caravan; it never breeds (pen_cap 1). It dies unfed.
horse_pen.theft: None: it is the player's own animal.
horse_pen.npc_note: Villagers neither keep nor slaughter it.
horse_pen.risk: Not at risk: one animal, bought.

pig_pen.name: Pigs
pig_pen.where: The pig pen south of the village
pig_pen.tool_hint: Not yours to take: the animals are their keeper's.
pig_pen.time_note: The keeper's slaughter is 30 game minutes.

action_cost.note: The keeper feeds the pen animals.pig.feed wheat a meal.

pig_pen.yield_notes: A young animal gives half the meat and no hide.
pig_pen.total: animals.pig.start in the pen, at most animals.pig.pen_cap.
pig_pen.regeneration: Litters while a well-fed pair shares the pen and it is under its cap; animals die unfed.
pig_pen.owner: The manor's pen, let to its keeper (a farmer); the animals are the keeper's.
pig_pen.theft: The player killing one is a crime against the keeper (main.gd _hit_animal).
pig_pen.npc_note: The keeper slaughters the surplus above animals.pig.keep (NPCBrain._keeper).
pig_pen.risk: Not at risk: pens hold at about their caps (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md).

sheep_pen.name: Sheep
sheep_pen.where: The sheep pen south of the village
sheep_pen.tool_hint: Not yours to take: the animals are their keeper's.
sheep_pen.time_note: The keeper's slaughter is 30 game minutes.

action_cost.note: The keeper feeds the pen animals.sheep.feed wheat a meal.

sheep_pen.yield_notes: A young animal gives half the meat and no hide. The manor's sheep give no wool: only a sheep in the player's own pen is shorn (wool, farming.products; PL2-015).
sheep_pen.total: animals.sheep.start in the pen, at most animals.sheep.pen_cap.
sheep_pen.regeneration: Litters while a well-fed pair shares the pen and it is under its cap; animals die unfed.
sheep_pen.owner: The manor's pen, let to its keeper (a farmer); the animals are the keeper's.
sheep_pen.theft: The player killing one is a crime against the keeper (main.gd _hit_animal).
sheep_pen.npc_note: The keeper slaughters the surplus above animals.sheep.keep (NPCBrain._keeper).
sheep_pen.risk: Not at risk: pens hold at about their caps (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md).

chicken_pen.name: Chickens
chicken_pen.where: The chicken pen south of the village
chicken_pen.tool_hint: Not yours to take: the animals are their keeper's.
chicken_pen.time_note: The keeper's slaughter is 30 game minutes.

action_cost.note: The keeper feeds the pen animals.chicken.feed wheat a meal.

chicken_pen.yield_notes: Chickens have no hide and lay no eggs: the game has no egg item. An adult gives feathers (animals.chicken.feathers; PL2-004), a trade good only: the game has no arrows, so the goods merchant is the one buyer. A young one gives none.
chicken_pen.total: animals.chicken.start in the pen, at most animals.chicken.pen_cap.
chicken_pen.regeneration: Litters while a well-fed pair shares the pen and it is under its cap; animals die unfed.
chicken_pen.owner: The manor's pen, let to its keeper (a farmer); the animals are the keeper's.
chicken_pen.theft: The player killing one is a crime against the keeper (main.gd _hit_animal).
chicken_pen.npc_note: The keeper slaughters the surplus above animals.chicken.keep (NPCBrain._keeper).
chicken_pen.risk: Not at risk: pens hold at about their caps (LONG_RUN_SIMULATION.md).

player_field.name: Your field
player_field.where: Ground you own or lease, cleared and tilled by you
player_field.tool_hint: No tool to harvest. Tilling is by hand, or quicker and easier with the hand plough (workbench: 4 planks and 2 iron bars).
player_field.time_note: A cell takes farming.harvest_seconds real seconds to harvest, farming.till.hand or farming.till.plough to till and farming.sow_seconds to sow. Crops ripen after farming.crops days of growth at the season's rate (farming.season_rate): spring and summer full, autumn half, winter none.

action_cost.note: Harvesting costs nothing. Tilling a cell costs farming.till stamina (the hand plough wears one a cell).

player_field.yield_notes: Per ripe cell: its crop (the herb crop is the wild flower the sage buys) and seeds_back seed of the same crop (seed saving). Seed is also sold by the farmers and the food stall's merchant at farming.crops seed_price (taken from the seller's own stock: MERCH-01).
player_field.total: As many cells as the player clears and tills on ground they hold; each ripens again after it is sown again.
player_field.regeneration: A harvested cell is tilled soil again: sow it with a seed. Nothing grows or can be sown in winter.
player_field.owner: The player's, on ground the player owns or leases from the manor.
player_field.theft: Nobody else works it: the village's farmers only cut the manor's fields, and nothing of the player's can be stolen by walking over it. Leaving the lease or selling the ground gives the field up.
player_field.npc_note: No villager sows or cuts it.
player_field.range_note: The cell 0.9 tiles in front of the player (Use on it; not part of Gather mode).
player_field.risk: Not at risk: the player's crops are theirs alone and the manor's fields are untouched.

player_pen.name: Your pen
player_pen.where: A pen the player fenced on ground they hold, stocked from the keeper's pens
player_pen.tool_hint: No tool: use the pen's gate.
player_pen.time_note: Collecting is instant at the pen's gate. A well-fed adult makes its product each farming.products days (a hen an egg, a cow milk, a sheep wool), kept in the pen up to farming.product_cap.

action_cost.note: The animals eat their animals feed in wheat a meal from the trough (fauna.gd), as the keepers' do.

player_pen.yield_notes: Per animal per product period. Meat and hides come from slaughter as for any animal (the keeper's nodes).
player_pen.total: Up to animals pen_cap of each kind in each pen.
player_pen.regeneration: A well-fed pair breed as in the village's pens and the young grow through the life stages; the products come from adults only.
player_pen.owner: The player's pen and animals, bought from the keeper's real stock (coins to the keeper).
player_pen.theft: Nobody else's to take; killing your own animals is no crime.
player_pen.npc_note: No villager keeps or milks them.
player_pen.range_note: At the pen's gate (the trough cell).
player_pen.risk: Not at risk: bounded by product_cap and the animals' own pen caps.

prospect_clue.name: Prospecting clue
prospect_clue.where: Stains on open ground in the village (a rust-red stain, black streaks, green-stained pebbles, a glitter of flecks), placed from the world seed by Prospecting.generate (prospecting.json); each marks a search area of `radius` cells round the stain, not a deposit
prospect_clue.tool_hint: You need a prospector's kit to take samples (forged at an anvil: an iron bar, a plank and leather).
prospect_clue.time_note: sample_minutes (prospecting.json, 30) game minutes a sample for a villager, by the Mining mine_time effect; the player's is timed as a mining swing (Prospecting.player_secs).

action_cost.note: No stamina. The kit wears kit_wear a sample unless the Mining tool_wear_save effect spares it.

prospect_clue.yield_notes: One rock sample a cell sampled, counted mined_ore_sample; where it was taken goes with it (the holder's bag). It is worth nothing until a smith assays it (Prospecting.assay: a fee, a coal, the forge's time).
prospect_clue.total: samples_per_clue (4) samples a clue, one a cell of its area; about a third of the village's 15-cell blocks hold a clue (clue_percent), some over a mineral body (true_percent), the rest misleading.
prospect_clue.regeneration: None: a cell sampled stays sampled and a clue sampled out stays so (saved in prospecting.taken). The stain itself stays.
prospect_clue.owner: Nobody: the ground's minerals are nobody's (the manor's mining rights are only proposed, P1.2).
prospect_clue.npc_note: MIN-C: a prospector (job prospector) samples the nearest clue it has taken fewer than samples_per_visit samples from, carries up to carry_samples to a smith for assay, and reports finds to the manor (Prospecting.plan). MIN-D: a villager takes up prospecting by the labour market (Discovery.prospector_place, from mining capability 1), and the manor commissions surveys of clues on its job board (ManorWork survey: samples, assays, a report; paid for the labour).
prospect_clue.range_note: The cell under the player's feet, inside a clue's area (main.gd _prospect_targets): one sample a cell, so Gather mode's repeated harvest does not apply; each sample is a Use on a fresh cell.
prospect_clue.risk: A clue is a hint, not a deposit: sampling and assays cost time, coal and coins and may find nothing (WDR-022). MIN-D: a body is opened into an ordinary seam only by a trial pit dug within reach of it (Discovery.trial_dig); most pits miss and a clue takes a finite number.

open_pit.name: Open pit
open_pit.where: Staked on clear common ground of the village by the player (with a pickaxe or a shovel in hand) or by the manor (for a find no trial pit can reach any more): a square of size cells (open_pit.json) with a clear border and spoil heaps beside it; on the surface only (OD-29)
open_pit.tool_hint: Earth (topsoil, dirt, spoil) is dug with a shovel, the rock with a pickaxe (owner MIN-E-Q4). The carpenter makes shovels to order for the goods merchant (a haft fitted with the smith's blade at the workbench); the smith sells pickaxes, or forge one at the anvil (2 iron bars and a plank).
open_pit.time_note: Each layer's minutes a unit (open_pit.json layers: topsoil 20, dirt 25, spoil 30, stone 25) for a villager, by the Mining mine_time effect; the player's swing is timed as a mining swing (OpenPits.player_secs).

action_cost.note: No stamina. The layer's tool (a shovel for earth, a pickaxe for rock) wears `wear` (1) a unit unless the Mining tool_wear_save effect spares it; each unit earns `xp` (4) Mining xp.

open_pit.yield_notes: One unit a dig, of the layer the cell is down to: under every cell the same finite layers (open_pit.json: 2 topsoil, 3 dirt, 3 spoil, then 8 stone), counted dug_<item>. A cell is dug to its ring's depth (terraces: the edge 2 layers, the next ring 3, the middle 4); the ramp's cells stay walkable. Dug down to the rock, a cell (not the ramp) opens a prospecting body within expose_reach as an ordinary seam (Discovery.expose).
open_pit.total: A pit's whole ground (OpenPits.volume, counted pit_ground_<item> when it is staked): for a 5 x 5 pit 50 topsoil, 75 dirt, 27 spoil and 8 stone.
open_pit.regeneration: None: a pit's ground only falls as it is dug, and rises only by backfill (the earth put back, counted backfilled_<item>). No new pit appears by itself: one is staked by someone.
open_pit.owner: Its staker: the player's pit is the player's to dig; the manor's is dug only through its excavate job (ManorWork). The ground is common land: no rights are made (MIN-C-Q2).
open_pit.theft: Never theft: nobody digs another's pit outside the manor's job.
open_pit.npc_note: MIN-E: villagers dig the manor's pit through its excavate job (ManorWork.post_pits, plan, do_step: a load of carry_ore units into the job's load, the earth tipped on the pit's spoil heaps, stone to the works yard; paid at the quarry job's rate a unit). A miner whose ore is worked out takes it as it takes a trial pit (NPCBrain._miner).
open_pit.range_note: A pit cell beside the player, ahead or one of its neighbours (main.gd _pit_targets); a heap beside the player for tipping or taking earth. Each unit is a Use: Gather mode's repeated harvest does not reach pits (ResourceNodes.node_at finds seams, trees, plants, fields and animals).
open_pit.risk: Space: the village's dense ground holds few pit sites (66 on the static layout), so the manor stakes a pit only where a known find lies near one; a pit dug for a find may expose nothing (WDR-022). Whether topsoil, dirt, spoil, quarry stone and building blocks are different goods, and what earth is used for beyond backfill, are the owner's open questions (MIN_E_OPEN_PIT.md).

tunnel_rock.name: Tunnel rock
tunnel_rock.where: The rock beside the floor of an underground level (the adit gallery, the cave under the hill), under the hill's static rock with rock all round it and inside the level map's edge; never a seam's cell (OD-29: tunnels only below ground)
tunnel_rock.tool_hint: You need a pickaxe to cut rock, and a timber support standing within 2 cells (mine_works.json support.reach) of the face.
tunnel_rock.time_note: Each unit's minutes (mine_works.json cell: stone 30, spoil 25) for a villager, by the Mining mine_time effect; the player's swing is timed as a mining swing (MineWorks.player_secs).

action_cost.note: No stamina. The pickaxe wears `wear` (1) a unit unless the Mining tool_wear_save effect spares it; each unit earns `xp` (4) Mining xp.

tunnel_rock.yield_notes: One unit a cut from the rock face beside the cutter (MineWorks.dig): every rock cell holds the same finite units (mine_works.json cell: 3 stone, then 2 spoil), counted cut_<item>; the last unit opens the cell as floor of its level (its A* at once). Unsupported rock is not cut: a timber support must stand within support.reach cells.
tunnel_rock.total: Bounded by the hill: only rock under the hill's static rock with rock all round may be cut (Underground.under_rock), 5 units a cell; the books (MineWorks.ground_cut) count every unit cut.
tunnel_rock.regeneration: None: a cell cut through stays floor (saved in mine_works.opened); no rock grows back.
tunnel_rock.owner: Common rock, like the seams below: nobody owns a tunnel; whoever cuts a unit holds it (MIN-C-Q2: no mining rights are made).
tunnel_rock.theft: Never theft: the rock is no one's.
tunnel_rock.npc_note: MIN-F: a villager cuts by the same function as the player (MineWorks.dig with the villager as `who`). MIN-F2 (Q2): the manor posts one tunnel job at a time while its works lack stone and a sound support holds a face (ManorWork.post_tunnels, MineWorks.manor_face): a load of carry_ore units cut into the job's load and brought to the works yard, paid at the quarry job's rate a unit; a miner whose ore is worked out takes it as a trial or excavate job. The face is chosen by the works alone: hidden ore is unknown to everyone until a cut exposes it.
tunnel_rock.range_note: A rock cell beside the player below ground, ahead or one of its neighbours (main.gd _works_targets). Each unit is a Use: Gather mode's repeated harvest does not reach tunnel rock (ResourceNodes.node_at finds seams).
tunnel_rock.risk: MIN-F2: an excavated cell too weakly held (supports worn, few, far) may cave in at dawn (MineWorks.stability, collapse_chance): rubble refills it (spoil, dug out again); supports wear and fail unrepaired. Ventilation and lighting as needs are not simulated. The hill holds little rock beyond the galleries, so tunnelling is short; hidden ore lies in its deep rock (Underground.hidden).

nails.text: B14-07: forged from iron bars at the anvil (forge_nails) and used up building wooden stairs (4 a rim cell) and walkways (3 a rim cell) through a mountain's cliff rim.

topsoil.text: MIN-E: put back into an open pit cell whose last unit dug was topsoil (OpenPits.backfill, counted backfilled_topsoil): the pit's ground rises by it.
MIN-E: tipped onto the pit's spoil heaps and taken back from them (OpenPits.tip, take): a heap is a solid cell while it holds anything.

dirt.text: MIN-E: put back into an open pit cell whose last unit dug was dirt (OpenPits.backfill, counted backfilled_dirt).
MIN-E: tipped onto the pit's spoil heaps and taken back from them (OpenPits.tip, take).

timber_support.text: MIN-F: made at the sawhorse from a log and two planks (make_timber_support) and set up on the floor of an underground level with a mallet (MineWorks.place_support), used up (used_timber_support): rock within support.reach cells of a support may be cut.

ladder.text: MIN-F2 (Q4): made at the workbench from planks and nails (make_ladder) and set into a sunk shaft with a mallet (MineWorks.install_ladder), used up (used_ladder): the shaft becomes a way between two levels the level router uses. It wears like a support and is repaired with a plank and nails, or replaced when it has rotted through.

track_section.text: MIN-F: made at the workbench from planks and nails (make_track_section) and laid one a cell with a mallet on an underground floor or in the mine's yard (MineWorks.lay_track), used up (used_track_section): a minecart runs on it.

spoil.text: MIN-F2 (Q5): put back into a passage below ground a unit at a time, by the player's own hands or by a worker on the player's paid order (MineWorks.fill, ManorWork backfill; counted filled_spoil): full, the passage is blocked and holds the cells beside it a little; dug again, it comes back as spoil.
MIN-E: put back into an open pit cell whose last unit dug was spoil (OpenPits.backfill, counted backfilled_spoil).
MIN-E: tipped onto the pit's spoil heaps and taken back from them (OpenPits.tip, take).

ore_sample.text: Read by a smith at the forge for a fee, with a coal (Prospecting.assay, MIN-C): the sample is used up and its reading becomes a record its holder and the smith know.

coal.text: An assay at the forge burns assay.fuel (one coal) of the smith's (Prospecting.assay, MIN-C).

log.text: Household firewood: every household burns a log from its pantry each night; a household without one is cold (noted, stat burned_log).
Villagers buy a log for the pantry in the evening from a carpenter or the raw-goods merchant.
Bought by the manor for repairs and carried to the works yard (haul), then used up mending (mend).

plank.text: B14-07: wooden stairs (3 a rim cell) and walkways (2 a rim cell) built through a mountain's cliff rim in the world outside (with nails, a mallet and Carpentry 2).
Bought for repairs and public works, carried to the works yard (haul) and used up mending (mend).
Fence round family farmland (FARM-02, owner Q9): one plank per 3 fence cells of the plot's perimeter, the gate cell free (the player pen's rule), used up.

stone.text: Bought for repairs and public works or quarried for the manor (quarry job), carried to the works yard and used up mending (mend).
The gate of family farmland's fence (FARM-02, owner Q9): farm_plot.gate_stone stone (provisional, awaiting the owner), used up.

rubble.text: STONE-04: the rubble a dressing leaves, bought for repairs and public works like stone, carried to the works yard and used up mending; also taken as raw stone by fittings, the farmland gate and older building sites at the moment they use it (World.rubble_cover), never as an input to dressing.

iron_bar.text: Fittings and nails: bought for repairs and public works, carried to the works yard and used up mending.

wheat.text: Livestock feed: keepers and the player put wheat in a pen's trough; each animal eats its feed a meal.
Households cook pottage over the hearth from pantry wheat (the cook_pottage recipe, no station).
The manor buys farmers' surplus for its granary and gives it out as relief (haul jobs carry it).

oak_sapling.text: Planted by the player on free grass in front of them (the pack window's Plant button): a sapling that grows into a mature oak by the game clock.

pine_sapling.text: Planted by the player on free grass in front of them (the pack window's Plant button): a sapling that grows into a mature pine by the game clock.

apple_sapling.text: Planted by the player on free grass in front of them (the pack window's Plant button): a sapling that grows into an apple tree that fruits in summer and autumn (B14).

apple.text: Eaten from the pack, or from a household's pantry (NPCBrain.FOOD); sold to the food merchant (B14).

lockpick.text: Picks a locked chest: one attempt takes game time, may open the lock until dawn or snap the pick (used up); a seen attempt is a crime.

padlock.text: Fitted to the player's own chest (used up once): the chest is then locked or unlocked with the player's key.

hammer.text: The smith's tool: it wears 2 with every anvil recipe a villager smith makes (the player needs none).

wheat_seed.text: Sown on a tilled cell of the player's field: one seed a cell (used up).
Sown on a tilled cell of a villager household's farmland: one seed a cell (used up), the player's rule (FARM-03).

carrot_seed.text: Sown on a tilled cell of the player's field: one seed a cell (used up).
Sown on a tilled cell of a villager household's farmland: one seed a cell (used up), the player's rule (FARM-03).

potato_seed.text: Sown on a tilled cell of the player's field: one seed a cell (used up).
Sown on a tilled cell of a villager household's farmland: one seed a cell (used up), the player's rule (FARM-03).

herb_seed.text: Sown on a tilled cell of the player's field: one seed a cell (used up).
Sown on a tilled cell of a villager household's farmland: one seed a cell (used up), the player's rule (FARM-03).

flower_seed.text: Sown by the player on free village grass in front of them (the pack window's Plant button): used up, a young wild flower that bears propagation grow_seasons later.

red_berry_cutting.text: Planted by the player on free village grass in front of them (the pack window's Plant button): used up, a young red berry bush that bears propagation grow_seasons later, in its seasons.

blue_berry_cutting.text: Planted by the player on free village grass in front of them (the pack window's Plant button): used up, a young blue berry bush that bears propagation grow_seasons later, in its seasons.

code_sources.text: The villagers' starting stock (a one-time source: each job starts with its tools and some goods).
Each household's pantry starts with 3 pottage and start_household_wheat_per_member wheat a member.
With the shared manor farming switch on (FSE-12), the manor fields' farmers start with one wheat seed a field cell, shared among them.
Each bandit starts with a copper sword.
The granary starts with start_granary_days of the village's food in wheat.

imports.text: When the village's seams of an ore or coal are down to caravan_import_when_left, each smith buys up to this stock from the caravan.
When the village's stone is down to caravan_import_when_left, the caravan sells up to caravan_stone.load a visit to the raw-goods merchants.

Each caravan visit sells the seed sellers (the food stall) up to caravan_seed_per_visit seed, cuttings and flower seed, the scarcest first, towards this stock, from the merchant's own coins (Build 13 rule 3, MERCH-01).

DVW-B3-LUX: costly goods the traders of Wulstead and Higham-on-the-Way hold in their stock (settlements.json start; GAME EXPANSION, from beyond the map). On a visit day villagers with a taste for them and spare coin beyond their reserve buy some, and the player buys at the wagon, at value x luxury.markup, the coins going into the trader's till and leaving the village. Kept, never used up.

exports.text: Every second day (the nearer settlements' traders more often) the caravan buys what a merchant (up to its BUYS caps) or a smith (the caps below) holds above half the cap, at 0.8 x value, unless the village is short of food. It never buys the mine's raw output (iron ore, copper ore, gold ore, coal, stone: NPCBrain.NOT_EXPORTED); those it only sells to the village. The caravan is the traders of the five neighbouring settlements: each buys only what its settlement still wants and pays only from the coins in its own trader's till, so a surplus nobody wants or can be paid for stays on the shelf.

non_harvestable.what: Crates, barrels and the tavern's tables (village.json containers), and the chests inside buildings
non_harvestable.reason: Their owners' stock, not a node: nothing grows or is made there. Taking from one is theft; a tavern table holds a keeper's dish while the tavern is open.
A merchant's shop: goods are bought, or the stall's stock is stolen while its merchant is away.
A works site the manor's mend jobs repair and where elders take the air. It gives nothing: the game has no water item.

non_harvestable.what: Crafting stations (a home's hearth is an oven, its table a food-preparation table: Furniture.STATION_OF)
non_harvestable.reason: They turn materials into goods by recipes.json; they yield nothing themselves.

non_harvestable.what: The tavern counter, the armoury counter and the mine cart
non_harvestable.reason: Map stations with no recipe and no harvest: the tavern counter is where the tavernkeeper serves and villagers drink; the others are decorative.
Where livestock is fed (wheat in, nothing out); the animals in a pen are livestock nodes, the keeper's.
What the dead or a kill left: taken once, not a node.

non_harvestable.what: Decorative map tiles (flowers, cliffs and rock faces, worked-out seams, stumps' surroundings)
non_harvestable.reason: Map art with no game object behind it.

exceptions.reason: MIN-E: earth comes only from the finite ground of the open pits staked in the village (OpenPits: each cell's layers, counted pit_ground_ when staked); nothing brings more, and none is meant to: the ground is finite (WDR-022).
MIN-E: earth comes only from the finite ground of the open pits staked in the village (OpenPits); nothing brings more, and none is meant to.

MIN-E: spoil comes only from the finite ground of the open pits staked in the village (OpenPits) and, MIN-F, from the rock cut to extend the tunnels below ground (MineWorks, bounded by the hill); nothing brings more, and none is meant to.

MIN-F: built from cart parts at the workbench (build_minecart); it is not consumed but used: set down on track it becomes a cart of kind minecart (Carts, MineWorks.set_down_minecart) that hauls goods along the rails below ground and out to the mine's yard.

MIN-C: rock samples come only from the clues' finite search areas (samples_per_clue a clue, one a cell); nothing brings more, and none is meant to: once the village's clues are sampled out, new ground to read is MIN-D's (deeper strata, the larger map). The finite source is the design, not a gap.
A trade good (PL2-004): chickens drop feathers and the goods merchant buys them (NPCBrain.BUYS / OUTLETS), but the game has no arrows or bedding to use them in, so no recipe consumes them.

B14: built from cart parts (build_handcart) by the player, the carpenter and storefront households, and bought and sold; it is not consumed but used: pulled storage, parked at home or a cart hub, and households' market runs (carts in play, B14-06, game/scripts/core/carts.gd).

After the iron seams are worked out, the smiths' iron comes only by caravan.
After the coal seams are worked out, the smiths' coal comes only by caravan.

The mine's one gold seam (8 units, Mining 3) is the only source; the caravan does not bring gold, so once the seam is worked out gold ore, gold bars and gold rings come only from what villagers already hold. Scarce by design (Build 13).
After the copper seams are worked out, the smiths' copper comes only by caravan.
After the stone seams are worked out, stone comes only by caravan, to the raw-goods merchants.
